main_text.p: runt punctati, quare aliquem non sibi comparavit Hieronymus, qui tantum opus aggrediebatur, Hieronymus qui potentissimarum Matronarum opibus sustentabatur, qui varias regiones adi-bat, ut cum doctissimis Judæis conferret, &c. Quid dicam de Ecclesia Christiana, quæ eo tempore multos adhuc amplec-tebatur Judæos conversos, ipsum S. Epi-phanium Hieronymi amicissimum. Nec semel ita philosophatus est, sed sæpissimé. Viginti duo loca adnotavimus in Exer-citat. Biblicis, lib. 1. Exercit. 6. c. 2. & argumenta hinc adversus puncta col-legimus, ideo hæc satis. Consideran-dum præterea, S. Hieronymum dicere, [?]דבר[?] vocales in medio non habere. Non agnoscit S. Hieronymus alias vocales Hebraeorum, quàm [?]אהיה[?] quas multis locis vocales appellat, scriberetur [?]יהוה[?] juxta Hieronymum, vocales habe-ret in medio ut [?]יהוה[?] nec alias vocales agnovit Josephus, cùm di-xit nomen Dei constare ex quatuor vo-calibus. Si apiculi infra supraqve litte-ras

page.notes: The Hebrew words are printed in Hebrew letters, and my readings of them are uncertain, so each is marked [?]. The ink blot over "sustentabatur" obscures part of the word, though it is legible. The "ras" catchword sits at the right below the last line. Printed spellings such as "Hieronymus" and "Epi-phanium" are kept, while qv has been normalised to qu (qvæ→quæ) per the u/v rule. Printed "Viginti" and "Exercit." are kept as they appear.
